Kalua Pork (Hawaiian Slow-Roasted Pork)

Served at: Tiki Christmas at Pearl Harbor

Serves 10-12Prep 20 minCook 8-10 hours (oven) or 10-12 hours (slow cooker)

Kalua Pork is a cornerstone of Hawaiian luaus and celebrations, traditionally cooked in an underground oven (imu). For your Tiki Christmas at Pearl Harbor, this home-friendly version captures the smoky, tender essence of the original, bringing a taste of the islands to your festive table without digging a pit in your backyard. It's perfect for feeding a crowd and embodies the spirit of aloha.

Ingredients

  • 1 (8-10 pound / 3.6-4.5 kg) boneless pork shoulder (Boston butt)
  • 2 tablespoons Hawaiian red alaea sea salt (or coarse sea salt)
  • 2 teaspoons liquid smoke (hickory or mesquite)
  • 1 cup (240 ml) water or chicken broth
  • Optional: 4-6 large banana leaves, thawed if frozen
  • Optional: 1 head green cabbage, cut into wedges (for serving)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C).
  2. Rinse the pork shoulder and pat it dry thoroughly with paper towels.
  3. Using a sharp knife, poke several deep holes (about 1-2 inches / 2.5-5 cm deep) all over the pork shoulder.
  4. Rub the Hawaiian salt evenly over the entire surface of the pork, ensuring some salt gets into the holes.
  5. Drizzle the liquid smoke over the pork, again trying to get some into the holes.
  6. If using banana leaves, lay them out overlapping on a large baking pan or roasting pan to create a bed for the pork. Place the seasoned pork on top of the leaves, then wrap the leaves tightly around the pork.
  7. Wrap the entire pork bundle tightly with several layers of heavy-duty aluminum foil, ensuring no steam can escape. If not using banana leaves, wrap the seasoned pork directly in multiple layers of foil.
  8. Place the wrapped pork in the roasting pan. Pour the water or chicken broth into the bottom of the pan, around the foil-wrapped pork.
  9. Roast in the preheated oven for 8-10 hours, or until the pork is fall-apart tender. (Alternatively, you can cook this in a large slow cooker on low for 10-12 hours).
  10. Carefully remove the pork from the oven. Let it rest, still wrapped, for at least 30 minutes before unwrapping.
  11. Unwrap the pork, discarding the banana leaves and foil. The meat should be incredibly tender. Use two forks to shred the pork directly in the roasting pan, mixing it with the accumulated juices.
  12. Serve the Kalua Pork hot, traditionally with steamed rice and, if desired, steamed cabbage wedges.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, you can insert small pieces of bacon or fatback into the holes you poke in the pork before salting.
  • The liquid smoke is crucial for replicating the imu flavor; don't skip it.
  • Leftovers are fantastic in sandwiches, tacos, or even mixed into scrambled eggs.
